biography.plain_text: Petter Christian Grüner Sundt was a Norwegian shipowner and investor from Oslo. He inherited an interest in his grandfather's shipping business, Bergesen, and helped expand its gas-carrier operations with his cousin Morten. After selling his stake, he reinvested much of the proceeds in property through his own investment company, Sundt AS.

confidence.reason: Primary institutional history and direct interviews corroborate the facts, with contemporary reports supporting personal context.

long_biography.plain_text:
Petter Sundt ran his investment company with a two-person team, delegating daily management to Leiv Askvig while the two spoke at least once a day. He favoured limited borrowing and kept substantial reserves in interest-bearing investments and bank deposits. His partnership with Christian Ringnes included a joint acquisition of the hotel-property company Pandox.

Sundt was also a longstanding financial supporter of Norway's sea-rescue service. He and his company financed the first vessel in a new class of fast rescue craft, which entered service in 2007. The class was named after him and became a model for subsequent rescue boats.
